top_news.title: DeepSeek search and fetch – $0.75 per 1000 successful requests
top_news.dek: DeepSeek has launched Search and Fetch APIs to provide agents and RAG pipelines with real-time web access.
top_news.brief: The new Search API returns structured web results, while the Fetch API converts web pages into Markdown. Both endpoints are available via the standard DeepSeek API bearer authentication at a cost of $0.75 per 1,000 successful requests.
top_news.image_alt: DeepSeek API documentation interface showing search and fetch endpoints

top_news.title: Two German courts now hold Google liable for what its AI overviews say
top_news.dek: German courts are establishing a legal precedent that holds Google directly liable for false information generated by its AI search summaries.
top_news.brief: Following a Munich ruling, the Aachen Regional Court has determined that Google's AI-generated content is legally attributable to the company. The court held Google responsible after its AI falsely linked a doctor to criminal offenses. This emerging legal consensus treats AI overviews as Google's own content rather than neutral search results, significantly increasing the company's liability for hallucinations.
top_news.image_alt: A digital representation of a search engine interface displaying an AI-generated summary.

primary.title: Two German courts now hold Google liable for what its AI overviews say
primary.summary: Google tried to overturn a landmark Munich ruling on AI search liability by appealing, then quietly settled. The strategy isn't working. The Aachen Regional Court just applied the exact same reasoning in a new case where Google's AI falsely attributed criminal offenses to a doctor that actually involved someone else. A consistent legal view is forming across German courts, and it treats Google's AI answers as the company's own content. The article Two German courts now hold Google liable for what its AI overviews say appeared first on The Decoder.

primary.title: AI agents chasing a $465 train refund invented excuses, leaked medical data, and spammed an MP's office
primary.summary: Six AI agents were tasked with recovering £350 (about $465) for a canceled train ticket in an experiment. They resorted to invented excuses, lawsuit threats, and sharing confidential health data. One agent sent 187 messages in 15 days, including 50 to a British MP's office. None of the models secured the refund, but the researcher warns of "agentic flooding" if these assistants are deployed at scale. The article AI agents chasing a $465 train refund invented excuses, leaked medical data, and spammed an MP's office appeared first on The Decoder.

primary.title: Anthropics' Claude cracks a 25-year-old NSA cryptography mystery in under 30 minutes
primary.summary: Anthropic's AI model Claude has solved a 25-year-old cryptography puzzle. The mysterious seeds behind NIST's standard curves for digital signatures were provided by the NSA without explanation, raising long-standing suspicion about built-in backdoors. Claude figured out in under 30 minutes that the seeds came from "lrand48," a simple C random number generator, making deliberate backdoors far less likely. The article Anthropics' Claude cracks a 25-year-old NSA cryptography mystery in under 30 minutes appeared first on The Decoder.
